chains.title: SPDEF ref-allele binding with altered TOX3 regulation by the alt allele

links.claim: SPDEF is proposed to bind the ref G allele more strongly. SPDEF has an own QBiC-SELEX model with a clear ref-favoring change (z -7.0, effect -0.244) and a strong ref site at the 99.7th percentile; SPDEF is occupied over the variant by ENCODE ChIP-seq in MCF-7 and is highly expressed in MCF7 (72.51 TPM, rank 40/1626). This is the strongest TF-binding evidence among the candidate chains.
The variant lies in the ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer-like region and in an SPDEF-bound ENCODE ChIP-seq peak in MCF-7; the nearest cCRE is nearby but does not directly overlap the SNP.

The element is proposed to regulate TOX3 in cis because TOX3 is the nearest protein-coding gene and has breast-cancer literature support. This remains proximity- and literature-based: GTEx reports no significant single-tissue eQTL, and no direct regulatory assay connects this element or SNP to TOX3.
SPDEF is highly expressed in MCF7 and its ChIP peak covers the variant in MCF-7, directly supporting an MCF7 breast-cancer cell context.

If SPDEF regulates TOX3, the alt allele's weaker SPDEF binding would alter TOX3 regulation and potentially breast cancer risk or progression. This is not established: the exact SNP lacks GWAS/Open Targets association, no GTEx eQTL is reported, and the SPDEF-TOX3 repression literature search did not return direct support (E36/E36a).

predictions: The ref G allele increases SPDEF occupancy at this element relative to the alt A allele.
The alt A allele reduces SPDEF binding and, if SPDEF regulates TOX3, changes TOX3 expression; the direction depends on whether SPDEF represses or activates TOX3.
SPDEF knockdown or overexpression should change TOX3 expression if this element is a functional SPDEF-responsive TOX3 enhancer.
falsified_if: The ref allele does not show higher SPDEF binding in allele-specific assays.
SPDEF perturbation has no effect on TOX3 expression.
The SPDEF ChIP peak over the variant is shown to depend on another site in the element rather than this base.

chains.title: TCF7L2 alt-allele gain-of-binding at a TOX3 enhancer

links.claim: TCF7L2 is proposed to bind the alt A allele more strongly. QBiC-SELEX detects an alt-favoring change (z 12.52, effect +0.745) and the alt site reaches the 97.8th percentile, and TCF7L2 has an MCF-7 ENCODE ChIP peak over the variant. However, E35 shows TCF7L2 has only CIS-BP-mapped models here (best mapped model TCF7L1), not an own TCF7L2 model, and TCF7L2 expression is low (4.89 TPM, rank 642/1626), so allele-specific action through this exact base is weak evidence.

The variant lies in the ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer-like region and in TF-bound chromatin; the nearest cCRE is a dELS 38 bp away, and many ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain this base, indicating an active regulatory element even though no cCRE directly overlaps the SNP.

The element is proposed to regulate TOX3 in cis because TOX3 is the closest protein-coding gene at 17.6 kb and is implicated in breast cancer literature. This is not established: GTEx v8 reports no significant single-tissue eQTL for this SNP, and no 3C, reporter, MPRA or CRISPR evidence is provided.

MCF7 is a breast cancer cell line in which TCF7L2 is expressed at low but detectable levels and in which a TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak covers the variant, making an MCF7/breast-cancer enhancer mechanism plausible but not proven.

Altered TOX3 regulation is proposed to influence breast cancer risk or progression. The exact SNP has no GWAS Catalog or Open Targets association in the provided evidence, so the disease link is inferential from TOX3 literature rather than direct variant-level evidence.

predictions: The alt A allele increases TCF7L2 occupancy at chr16:52565398 in allele-specific binding assays.
TCF7L2 perturbation should change TOX3 expression if this element is TCF7L2-responsive and TOX3-linked.
The effect should be most plausible in MCF7 breast cancer chromatin, where a TCF7L2 ChIP peak covers the variant; TCF7L2 expression is low but detectable.
falsified_if: No allele-specific TCF7L2 binding is observed for G versus A in recombinant binding, MCF7 ChIP or reporter assays.
TCF7L2 perturbation does not affect TOX3 expression.
The TCF7L2 ChIP peak over the variant is shown to depend on a nearby site rather than this base.

chains.title: SLC2A4RG ref-allele binding at a TOX3 enhancer, with occupancy unknown

links.claim: SLC2A4RG is proposed to bind the ref G allele more strongly. Its own QBiC-SELEX model gives a very large ref-favoring effect (z -45.42, effect -4.513) with a strong ref site at the 99.9th percentile, and SLC2A4RG is highly expressed in MCF7 (148.81 TPM, rank 15/1626). However, ENCODE never assayed SLC2A4RG here, so there is no occupancy evidence; per the rules, a large QBiC-SELEX change without occupancy is only weak evidence for action at this base.
The variant lies in the ENSR16_9QTBS enhancer-like region and in TF-bound chromatin, so the element is active; SLC2A4RG occupancy of this specific element is unknown.
The element is proposed to regulate TOX3 by proximity and breast-cancer literature only. No GTEx eQTL, 3C, reporter, MPRA or CRISPR evidence directly links this SNP or element to TOX3.
MCF7 expresses SLC2A4RG highly, making a breast-cancer-cell mechanism possible, but there is no ChIP evidence that SLC2A4RG occupies this element in MCF7 or any other cell type.

If SLC2A4RG occupies and regulates TOX3, the alt allele's weaker SLC2A4RG binding could alter TOX3 regulation and breast cancer biology. This is highly inferential: the exact SNP has no provided GWAS/Open Targets association and no eQTL, and occupancy is untested.

predictions: SLC2A4RG binds the ref G allele much more strongly than the alt A allele in vitro.
If SLC2A4RG occupies this element in breast cancer cells, the ref allele should have higher SLC2A4RG occupancy.
SLC2A4RG perturbation should change TOX3 expression only if SLC2A4RG occupies and regulates this element.
falsified_if: SLC2A4RG shows no allele-specific binding for G versus A in vitro.
SLC2A4RG does not occupy this element in MCF7 or breast cancer cells.
SLC2A4RG perturbation does not affect TOX3 expression.

QBiC-SELEX screen of chr16:52565398:G>A, one line per TF, each with the TF's own or CIS-BP-mapped model of largest |z|. Candidates are TFs whose ENCODE ChIP-seq peaks contain the variant and that are expressed (DepMap line ACH-000019), bound here before bound elsewhere, then a strong site before a weak one, then by |z|; then expressed TFs ENCODE never assayed whose best model passes the gate (occupancy unknown). Shown: 10 of 79 occupied (16 with a strong site), 5 of 137 with unknown occupancy. Left out: 49 TFs assayed in the matching biosample and 425 assayed only elsewhere, none with a peak here; 20 bound but below 1 TPM. The gate (|z| > 4.05, Bonferroni over 997 models) marks a change QBiC-SELEX detects; it says nothing about occupancy. Effect > 0 means the alternate allele binds more strongly. In vitro binding only. Site strength is the better allele's best k-mer over the variant, as a percentile of the best model's k-mers; a strong site reaches the 97.5th. At a weak site the ChIP peak more likely reflects another site in the element.
